name: Falfarren River
summary: The Falfarren River runs through central Ashenvale, dividing night elven lands from Horde outposts. Travelers meet wild dangers and open conflict along its banks.

sections.title: A Contested Natural Boundary
sections.body:
From Mount Hyjal, the Falfarren River spills over waterfalls into Xavian. Then it winds between Splintertree Post and Night Run. In ordinary weather, the water is neither especially deep nor hard to cross.

The river marks a rough boundary through central Ashenvale. Astranaar and the heart of the Kaldorei lands lie west, while Horde camps and lumber operations lie east. Wooden bridges on the main road carry travelers into the contested forest, where patrols clash along the banks.

sections.title: Hazards in the Shallows
sections.body:
The Falfarren River brings dangers beyond clashes between sentinels and grunts. Near Felfire Hill, corrupted bog beasts and aggressive water creatures prowl the muddy shallows. Rain can swell the currents.

Dense canopies line both shores, where ambushes and skirmishes often spill into the stream.

faq.q: Where does the Falfarren River begin and end?
faq.answer: The Falfarren River begins in the heights of Mount Hyjal and tumbles over waterfalls into the lake at Xavian. It winds southwest across Ashenvale, then disappears underground beneath the northern mountains of the Barrens.

faq.q: Why is the Falfarren River significant to the war in Ashenvale?
faq.answer: The Falfarren River marks a rough boundary between night elf and Horde control in central Ashenvale. Astranaar lies west, while the orc outpost of Splintertree Post and active Horde lumber operations lie east.

faq.q: What threats should travelers expect along the riverbanks?
faq.answer: Aggressive bog beasts prowl the shallows, especially near the corrupted lands around Felfire Hill. Alliance and Horde patrols watch bridges and crossings, and skirmishes or ambushes can break out along the banks.

angles.text: As a Night Elf or ally, crossing east over the Falfarren River brings you to the Horde's front lines near Splintertree Post.
As a member of the Horde, the Falfarren River marks the western edge of your expansion from Splintertree Post. Fortified night elf territory lies beyond it.
